title: CIA Character Record Schema
rules: Record first/last as first/last currently recovered evidence, never lifetime endpoints unless independently established.
Do not infer motive, diagnosis, criminality, supernatural status or permanent moral essence from a role label.
Project-symbolic debt, karmic debt and spiritual accounting are not legal or financial liabilities unless independently established.
Association is typed: co-presence is weaker than direct interaction, and direct interaction is weaker than an explicit relationship claim.
Keep user-supplied alias clues separate from independently recovered aliases.
A role can change; retain old and new states with dates instead of overwriting history.
Visual activity fading reflects archive recency/status only, never moral value or human worth.
A Dooley Welfare counter may run only when a dossier explicitly enables it with a start date and rate; it is display-only project fiction, not money.
Portraits/evidence images require an explicit dossier-owned source reference; never guess a real person's identity from an unsourced image.
Shared symbolic proxy images must be labeled as non-likeness role illustrations and may not be presented as portraits or documentary evidence.
Every mature dossier should explain why it matters and separate known material, interpretation and unknowns before adding more labels.
Thin dossiers may become more meaningful by preserving exact presence windows and explicit missing context rather than inventing incidents.
Tim's character assessments must remain explicitly attributed to Tim or another named source; archive synthesis must be labeled as synthesis rather than direct quotation.
Clinical-sounding terms such as narcissistic or delusional may be preserved only as attributed non-clinical characterizations unless an independent qualified diagnosis is actually sourced.
Truthful/dishonest and trustworthy/untrustworthy labels require a dated statement, contradiction, admission or repeated reliability pattern; disagreement alone is not enough.
Preserve changing assessments over time rather than overwriting an earlier role or character judgment.
